rv.t: A place I would like to come back to. The charm is in the hiking trail, that goes from Eze, and there are two to choose from. Spectacular views.

Fort de la Revère is one of the most breathtaking spots on the French Riviera. Perched high above the sea, it offers a panoramic view stretching from Monaco to Cannes. The old military fort adds a touch of history, while the surrounding park is peaceful, filled with the scent of pine and wild herbs. Perfect for hiking, picnics, or just clearing your mind. Easy to reach from Èze or La Turbie — and absolutely worth…
Awesome views. The fort is closed but the views are great. Free parking just beside. Be aware of clouds and low visability alle days.

rv.t: This is a small, simple hotel that's perfectly located to walk to the beach, train station, tram, bars, restaurants, and shops. Based on our stays in other European hotels, we'd say this is a 3-star hotel. We booked a deluxe room, which we thought was very small and basic and badly in need of an upgrade. The orange carpet, basic dark furniture, and peeling wallpaper looked really tired and dated. The beds and…

Lovely friendly reception staff. The room was simple, clean and quiet. Great bed - I slept really well. Good breakfast and great coffee. The location is fantastic. Quiet but very close to the beach and surrounded by bakeries, shops, bars and restaurants. I was there for work but a local colleague took me all over Nice and we walked everywhere. Safe was too small for a laptop and replacement water was missed a couple…

This is definitely not a four star hotel. I’ve never had to get my own water and towels at the receptionist, and bring all my luggage to the room with no help from the team at all. Plus, the hallways smell like sewage, And the bedsheets are not clean. Some of the receptionists are nice, but some are just very unwelcoming.

The website photos are completely not accurate. This is an old and outdated hotel. The halls are dark. Flirting is old and there is even an odd smell in the rooms. The location is centrally located so if the rest doesn’t bother you then you’re…

Very disappointing experience for a 4-star hotel. We booked a city-view room through Agoda and expected a queen-size bed, but were assigned a twin room on the ground floor instead. While checking the room, we found that one of the beds had not been properly prepared and was missing bed sheets. The room telephone was also broken, making it impossible to contact reception from the room. When we reported these issues…

rv.t: overcrowded - busy waiting room and long queues at the ticket office. rude and unhelpful staff. no outdoor seating other than those belonging to the cafes which require a purchase. one of the stairways to the platforms (the one to the right) is closed so good luck if you're running late and happened to turn right!

1. Buying a ticket takes forever. The machines are very slow and lines are long. Note to gare nice ville: find a way to make express booths for people who know where they want to go. 2. Finding the train platform is a mess: they have one screen at the entrance that shows the train platform letter with the destination. After you buy your tickets, no screen or direction at all. This station and the trains that service this beautiful part of France get worse eveytime we visit Nice and are an absolute disgrace. There is no ticket office, the staff are generally rude and the ticket machines - those that are working - that you are forced to use are hopelessly difficult causing long queues. So we ended up missing the train having taken 20 minutes just to buy a ticket. We then wait on the…

rv.t: Such a beautiful place! Nice Port is absolutely charming and definitely one of the highlights of the city. I love the atmosphere here with all the boats and the classic architecture surrounding the docks. It's a great spot for a walk and to soak in the Mediterranean vibes. Make sure to check out my 360° photo to get the full view of this amazing harbor!

Separated from the Old Town by a headland, it would be easy to miss visiting the port. However, that would be a shame as there are many fine boats in the marina to look at, and cafes in the area. It also has a very useful tram terminus which is just a short walk from the ferry dock.
Nice marina with some impressive yachts. This is a good walking area with much less tourists than in the city center. I enjoyed it very much.

rv.t: Super great view a must! If you visit Nice this attraction spot is you can see outlook view point of the port and beach side. Highly recommend!!! To visit. Should spend half day over here and there are walkway down the beach too.

Beautiful, you will get a lot of steps in. I think there are tours available on golf cart trains if you don’t want to climb. There are no clear directions so we had to depend on asking others. It’s worth visiting for sure.

The views at Colline du Château were absolutely breathtaking. Almost every corner was Instagram-worthy, making it such a beautiful place to explore and take photos. We ended up staying for quite a while because of the stunning panoramic views overlooking the Promenade des Anglais, the city, and Port Lympia on the other side. Despite the number of tourists around, the atmosphere still felt serene and peaceful. The…

rv.t: We visited Sunset Café in Nice and were absolutely delighted. The venue is located right on the promenade with a stunning sea view, creating a unique atmosphere of relaxation and romance. The interior is stylish and cozy, while the staff are attentive and friendly. We especially enjoyed the fresh dishes and their beautiful presentation. Everything was prepared with great care, quality, and attention to detail.

Just had a super dinner here. Called and reserved as it’s a Sunday. Lovely service, gracious staff. Gorgeous oysters, reasonable price and delicious Sea bass filets cooked really well with a lovely butter sauce on the side, roasted Grenaille potatoes. Crème brûlée dessert with a perfect crunchy top. The Chardonnay was lovely and peachy. Thoroughly recommend a visit here. Contrary to an earlier review.. toilet us…

All in all, the food here tasted quite good. The burgers are nice and tasty, the meat is tender and well cooked... All in all good taste. As for the Wok's, we wouldnt recommend ordering it, as it tasted and looked quite un-authentic. If you go here, stick to the meat and fish, and you'll have a great time. The tapas are also quite good. Local and good food. We had a good time here. Also: Good music playing ;)

2177.aj: Maison Gannac citrus groves, 2970 Rte de Super Garavan, 06500 Menton, フランス

rv.t: A True Citrus Paradise in Menton! Visiting Maison Gannac was an absolutely brilliant experience. The panoramic view of the coast is simply breathtaking. We want to send a special thank you to Celine, the administrator. She is an incredibly lovely, warm woman who hosted a truly unforgettable tasting for us! All of their products—the liqueurs, jams, and oils—are of the highest quality, with a spectacular, authentic…

Did a tour with Celine. It was a lovely tour that teaches you about the history of their farm, lemons, and a tasting of citrus infused jams and alcohol. Would highly recommend. Note, it’s a bit windy driving up, and I would highly recommend anti motion sickness meds if you’re prone to that.

I visited on April 2nd and had a wonderful afternoon. The hostess was incredibly warm, friendly, and funny—she went above and beyond to share the history of citrus with us in English. We also got to sample the fresh fruits, lemonade, jams, and liqueurs. It was such an interesting tour and a truly memorable experience. Highly recommended!

rv.t: A great market open from as early as 5:00am but most stalls are closed by around 1:00pm, so get there early. Many of the stalls are artisan by nature. The produce in most stalls is exceptional. We go most days for fresh bread and morning pastries.
A great market on Saturday morning. Do try to go there early. You'll find fresh vegetables, cheeses and meats. Outside the market sells household goods, clothing and plants.

Great market, lots of options and vendors. So much to tempt you! All the food is local and it’s great to be able to buy exactly what you need instead of the pre packaged stuff we are stuck with the UK. Go early and spend some time browsing!

One can choose during the 2 hours session and after little introduction 5-6 base notes from 128 notes on your olfactory organ, 3-4 heart notes and 2-3 top notes, and create this way your own perfume exactly to your taste. rv.t: Parc Phœnix is a really enjoyable experience and great value for money, with entry costing around €6. There is plenty to see, including crocodiles, wallabies, otters, flamingos, insects, snakes, porcupines, peacocks, chickens, goats and more. The animals all appeared well cared for which was nice to see. One of the highlights is the indoor area with large glass ceilings, which creates a really unique environment…

Beautiful gardens, and interesting smaller animals to see, can't believe it was only €5.50 entry! I loved the Tamarins, my husband liked the crocodiles, and we both liked the otters and chickens! We visited earlier today - a Tuesday in late May, by tram (very easily accesible from Nice), and it was quiet. Unfortunately the Museum of Asian Arts is closed on Tues. N.B. it is right next to the airport, so expect some…

Amazing! What great value, our kids were free and we were only €5.50 each to get in. If this was in the UK it would be about £25-30 each, if not more..! But that becomes irrelevant the moment you step onto the Croisette side and feel the pulse of the Cannes Film Festival. This is where the world’s most influential voices in film, media, and culture converge — where careers shift, deals close, and stories move from idea to…

Great experience at Palais des Festivals et des Congrès while attending World AI Cannes Festival. The venue is modern, well organized, and perfectly located by the harbor. It’s exciting to be in such an iconic place. Definitely worth a visit when in Cannes!

rv.t: Absolutely amazing views from the top of the ruined citadel, looking over the village of Entrevaux and the Var valley. It costs 5 euros to enter and the climb up to it takes around 20 minutes up several zigzagging ramps, which are made of slightly uneven stones so you should wear walking shoes if possible. It also has a number of old prison cells at the top, which used to house captured German soldiers in WW1. It…
5€ entrance fee, a nice, not very demanding hike up the hill, could use some cleaning but in general a very nice experience!

Visiting Entrevaux feels like exploring Minas Tirith from “The Lord of the Rings”! Winding, narrow, cobbled streets. Arched gateways and hidden squares. Staircases that spiral up into the shadowed heights. And towering over it all the Citadel. A magical place to wander around for a few hours.

rv.t: The food is fantastic! Not only is it delicious, but the portion sizes are also very generous and more than satisfying, especially the seafood spaghetti. The staff is incredibly polite, professional, and welcoming. Even when the restaurant is very busy, they remain friendly, attentive, and always greet guests with a smile. Overall, a wonderful dining experience that I would highly recommend!

Great ambience. It occupies a massive portion of the sidewalk in a market center type area. Servers could smile a bit more and make guests more comfortable. Food options are good. Get spaghetti based food if you are hungry. The steaks are very small
Nice offer of cocktails, service nice and not so slow. You are here mostly for the atmosphere of Cours de saleya. (But next time i prefer to go to the bars in Vieux Nice)

Wonderful shop and vine bar! Excellent service by Belinda😊we got a private tour of the vine cellar! This place is so beautiful and if you are looking for great vine and atmosphere you must pay a visit🙌🏼/Camilla from Stockholm
Awesome wine tasting experience at Nice’s Cave Bianchi. The host and his team were warm, friendly, and charming! I recommend this stop when in Nice.

rv.t: Sat at the second floor with the superb sea view. Love it! However, it allows smoking hence kinda irritating for us when people besides smoke. But the view compensates for that and the food is delicious and staff are very nice and friendly. Price is also reasonable. Just one thing is that the free bread that they provide is the worst I had in Franch so far. Simply did not touch it after first bite.

We got some incredible drinks and some pretty darn. Good food, sitting right at the balcony bar. Looking out onto the beach while the world was moving and the city was grooving. We were above it. All saw a live band two doors down from outside. Our waitress was a nice French woman who helped us out with the menu. We really appreciate the service.
